fixes.explanation: Paul says it plainly: “…death was passed on to all men, because all sinned.” (Romans 5:12) Adam, the first man (1 Corinthians 15:45), is where it started, but he isn't the only name on the list. Hold onto your hat, friend, because the good news is coming.

Paul says death reigned from Adam until Moses. Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is the one the law came through (John 1:17). So Paul's point is that death was already reigning before the law was given (Romans 5:13-14). Nobody had to write it up for death to show up.

Noah, who built the ark as God commanded him (Genesis 6:22), is a great name, but Paul doesn't use it here. He says death reigned from Adam until Moses. Moses is the marker because that's where the law comes into the picture. Good guess, friend, just a different stop on the timeline.

David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), is a fine name, but Paul doesn't use it here. Paul says death reigned from Adam until Moses. He's talking about the stretch before the law was given. Moses is the name on Paul's ticket.

Paul says the opposite. Death reigned “…even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed.” (Romans 5:14) So death's reach went past the people who sinned in the way Adam transgressed. It's a bigger reign than that.

That's right, and here's what Paul says: death reigned “…even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed.” (Romans 5:14) Death didn't keep a guest list. It reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way Adam transgressed.

Paul's words are “…how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many!” (Romans 5:15) The trespass was real, but grace goes further. That makes me want to wave my mustache.

Paul's word is justification: “…the gift that followed many trespasses brought justification.” (Romans 5:16) It's the opposite of condemnation. Think about that: the gift followed many trespasses, not just one. Now that's a gift worth unwrapping, friend.

Paul says it just that way: “…those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!” (Romans 5:17) Death reigned through one man, and those who receive will reign in life through another. Notice the word receive, friend. It's a gift, so the job is to take it.

Paul really does say it: “…those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!” (Romans 5:17) Death reigned through one man, and those who receive will reign in life through the other. It's a gift, so the job is to receive it.
